Grace/Ben — draft threat summary attached (see comments). Key items I called out: 

1) Sidecar mTLS bypass (abuse case):
   - Scenario: compromised operator container attempts to hijack sidecar channel to access KV cache or request-injection.
   - Controls: per-pod mTLS with workload identities, mutual TLS with short-lived certs, CNI-level policy to prevent host-networked containers from reaching sidecar port space.
   - Evidence: sample mTLS handshake log (attached), description of cert rotation cadence.

2) KV cache exfiltration via prefix lookup abuse:
   - Scenario: adversary runs crafted prompts to induce high-probability prefix probes to enumerate cache entries.
   - Controls: prefix scoping, LRU-based cache eviction limits per tenant, tokenized cache keys, rate-limiting at the router.

3) Control-plane impersonation / replay:
   - Scenario: attacker with stale control-plane tokens tries to roll a model or change routing to a vulnerable variant.
   - Controls: signed rollout manifests, revocation lists, enforcement at the dataplane gateway, operator auditing + immutable change events.

4) Egress lateral movement via shared infra:
   - Scenario: east-west movement from one tenant path into operator management plane or shared telemetry store.
   - Controls: sealed subnets, strict egress allowlists per tenant, dedicated telemetry ingestion endpoints with tokenized ingestion keys.

I added annotated mitigations and a short mapping to our standard evidence packets (SOC2 artifacts, flow logs, draw.io). Ben — diagram to attach and I'll incorporate into the final PDF.

Irene

Samantha — attaching the initial packet for your review. Files included (stubs):

- redwood_runtime_controlplane_dataplane_v1.png (PNG, 1.2MB) — control-plane vs data-plane diagram covering Hosted API and Private VPC flows, sidecar placement, operator paths.
- mTLS-sidecar-annotated.drawio (source) — annotated arrows for mTLS lanes and trust boundaries.
- empire_threat_summary_comments_v1.pdf (PDF, 2 pages) — enumerated abuse-cases, mitigations, evidence pointers.
- evidence_flow_log_snippet.txt (text) — sanitized VPC flow log snippet showing a successful mTLS handshake and a blocked lateral attempt (redacted IPs).

Notes/highlights:
- Mutual TLS with workload identities is enforced between runtime processes and sidecars; cert rotation is automated (15m TTL for session certs, 24h for workload certs).
- Sidecar ports are reachable only from the tenant pod network and the dataplane gateway; operator commands require signed manifests and pass through a read-only operator control API that cannot directly access runtime KV keys.
- KV cache keys are namespaced and tokenized; we additionally enforce per-tenant rate limits and probe-detection rules that throttle anomalous prefix-lookup patterns.

Links / evidence:
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1A2bExampleDriveLink/view (diagram + source + PDF)
- HubSpot ticket: HS-87933 (RFI for Empire Health)

Thanks — Grace
